faq_sources.topic: Are there special rules for roofs in Port Royal's Old Village?
answer_facts: Not found by name: no Town source I read uses 'Old Village' as a regulated district or sets roof-specific standards (tried: Port Royal Code Art. 3 s.3.3.50, zero hits for 'Old Village'; Historic Preservation Committee page; HPC application; Building Official page).

What exists: the Town's Historic Preservation Overlay (HPO) Zone, Port Royal Code Art. 3 s.3.3.50. A Certificate of Appropriateness 'may be required for alteration, construction, demolition, or relocation on property listed on the Town Historic Register visible from a public street right-of-way'; visible 'even if hidden by vegetation or a fence'; 'any change to a landmark may require a certificate even if not visible'.
Exempt from a certificate: 'Repairs, replacements, and routine maintenance that do not constitute alteration' and 'Exterior painting of previously painted structures'.

The Commission may authorize the Administrator (with chairman concurrence) to approve certain work; the Administrator may approve items 'not so significant as to impair or affect historic, architectural, or aesthetic character' within 15 days; otherwise the Historic Preservation Commission (5 members, 3rd Tuesday 3:00 pm, 700 Paris Ave) decides.

Applications judged on the Secretary of the Interior's Standards. Town's list of designated landmarks/districts is maintained by the Municipal Clerk (code) / Planning Office ('Port Royal Historic Landmark List' document, not retrieved). Whether a given Old Village house is on the Register is a per-address check with Planning, 843-986-2207.
Demolition-by-neglect clause lists 'Deterioration of roofs' as an example of exterior deterioration for Register properties.
Building permits: Town Building Official page says permits via Permits Administrator 843-986-2219 / permits@portroyal.org; page does not mention re-roof.
sources: https://www.portroyal.org/DocumentCenter/View/116/Article-3---Specific-to-Zones-PDF (Port Royal Code Art.3 s.3.3.50, undated scan; read 2026-10-12)

faq_sources.topic: Do you work on homes near Parris Island and in military housing? (public facts only)
answer_facts: Parris Island was annexed by the Town of Port Royal on Oct 11, 2000, 'effectively doubling the municipal population overnight due to on-base housing' (Wikipedia).

Laurel Bay is an unincorporated census-designated place in Beaufort County, ZIP 29906, a military housing complex opened in the mid-1950s that serves families at MCAS Beaufort, MCRD Parris Island and Naval Hospital Beaufort (Wikipedia).

On-base housing at MCAS Beaufort is privatized (PPV, Public Private Venture); the partner is HUNT Military Communities at Tri-Command, serving MCAS Beaufort, MCRD Parris Island and Naval Hospital Beaufort (Military OneSource). The same page still says 'AMCC at Tri-Command' once (older name). Search results (not fetched; marines.mil returned 403) say day-to-day management is by Tri-Command Property Management as Hunt's agent and that Laurel Bay Family Housing is a Hunt property.

Implication: on-base privatized homes are maintained by the housing partner, so an individual homeowner does not hire a roofer for them; off-base homes near the bases are ordinary private property. Whether Apex does any military-housing work is a client fact (not answered).
Military Housing Office, MCAS Beaufort: (843) 228-6000; Parris Island housing office numbers differ across pages.

faq_candidates.question: My Port Royal house is in a flood zone - does a big re-roof or remodel trigger the 50% elevation rule?
faq_candidates.why_this_town: The Town's own Citizen's Guide to Flood Awareness and local flood damage prevention ordinance; town elevation 3 ft (Wikipedia). Caveat: the 50% substantial-improvement rule is the NFIP baseline, so only the Town's application is local; portability is borderline.
answer_facts: Town guide: FEMA flood maps 'adopted as part of our local flood damage prevention ordinance'.

'If additions, remodeling or repairs to an existing structure equals or exceeds 50% of the building's market value, the entire building must be elevated above the base flood elevation' (same for substantial damage).

Elevation Certificates for new or substantially improved structures by a registered land surveyor or engineer; certificates on file available on request; building permit required before construction in flood zones.

Guide is undated; contact numbers inconsistent (Building Code Office (843) 986-2215; flood insurance info (843) 986-2207). The Town's ordinance PDF was not read, so the cumulative-cost look-back period for Port Royal is NOT FOUND.

faq_candidates.question: Is my home in Shell Point or Burton inside the Town of Port Royal, and who handles my roof permit?
faq_candidates.why_this_town: Port Royal annexed Shell Point, Burton and Parris Island (Wikipedia), so addresses with a Beaufort mailing address can be in the Town. Borderline: touches the permit topic Bluffton owns; use only if Paul accepts a which-office angle.
answer_facts: 'Port Royal also annexed properties in the Shell Point and Burton areas of Beaufort County' (Wikipedia).
Town Building Department: permits via Permits Administrator 843-986-2219, permits@portroyal.org, 700 Paris Ave. County building-codes page lists Port Royal under 'Municipalities' separately.
Per-address check: Town of Port Royal / Beaufort County GIS (not retrieved).
